findings.description: debtKind only replaces `\d+` inside a matched figure span. A coverage-gap percentage that moves between a whole number and a decimal ("71%" vs "71.3%") therefore gives different kinds ("#%" vs "#.#%"), and the re-gate files a duplicate ledger entry for a flag already held. The old whole-description `\d+` had the same gap. Normalise `\d+(?:\.\d+)?` instead.

The decision 86 amendment's example `(patch coverage 71.0% below baseline 80.0%)` can't occur. `pct` in src/core/debt.service.ts:391 (`Math.round(ratio * 1000) / 10`) never writes a trailing `.0`, so the real text is `71%` / `80%`.

The comment "A merged session has no window to steer: accepting the debt is its only way through (decision 86)" restates the new `MergeOutcome.regated` JSDoc, which already says the session has no window to steer and cites decision 86 (general.md §Comments: a call-site comment that restates the callee's JSDoc is a duplicate). It also contradicts the message below it, which offers "or fix it on the branch, push, then re-gate". Delete it.

The `DEBT_FIGURES` regexes pin the exact wording of flag descriptions built in src/core/debt.service.ts, with no compile-time link. If that wording changes, the figures stop being normalised, and every re-gate where a figure moved files a duplicate ledger entry. The it.each held-flag tests catch some rewordings, but `debtKind` has no direct test.

`measureBranch`'s acceptHint decides it is a re-gate from `session.state === 'merged'`, while the CLI now uses `MergeOutcome.regated`, so there are two sources of truth for the same fact. They agree today because only `regateMerged` reaches `measureBranch` with a merged session.

The new flag-only re-gate refusal message repeats the `--accept-debt "<reason>" --review-by "<condition>"${approvedByHint}` clause from the plain refusal below it, and the "Re-gate refused: … vouches for the earlier pin only" prefix from the failed-stage branch above it.

The decision 86 amendment's "Tests:" sentence is a long run-on that lists test cases the test files already state, so it will go stale as the tests change. Keep the behavioural rules and drop the test inventory.
